name: MoSPI: IIP, WPI, NAS, CPI (reference)
note_why: A reference pipeline (signals/README, MoSPI; COMPOSITION_SPEC §24): saved releases, a consolidated CSV and a gate, but no compute module, no skeleton, no system model and no signals of its own. Its only consumer is the 1f family on the credit pipelines that declare depends_on: ["mospi"]. order 0 because a pipeline's order must come after everything it depends on (test_manifest), and every credit pipeline may depend on this one.

api.note_why: page_size: 200 is the largest the API accepts (300 → HTTP 400, probed 2026-09-28 on all three endpoints). The server needs TLS legacy renegotiation, which OpenSSL 3 refuses by default; mospi_api enables it for this host only.

iip.note_why: Lag: July 2026 was released 28 Aug (MoSPI calendar: the 28th of M+1).

wpi.note_printed_growth: WPI prints no growth rate on the API: every WPI series is counted as no_printed_rate.
wpi.note_why: base_year=2022-23 is UNDOCUMENTED and load-bearing: without it the API serves the 2011-12 series with status 200. The 953 items (rows with `item` set, ~85% of the volume) are dropped at fetch because nothing reads them: a declared decision, not an accident. Lag: August 2026 was released 14 Sep.

nas.note_no_printed_rate: MoSPI prints quarterly growth only for GVA (indicator 21) and GDP (22); indicators 1-34 enumerated 2026-09-28. PFCE is counted as no_printed_rate.
nas.note_why: frequency_code is honoured; `frequency` is silently ignored (282 rows, annual mixed in), which is why every filter is verified on the rows. Without base_year one response mixes both bases. The growth indicators (21, 22) carry the printed rate in the price columns. Lag: Q1 FY27 was released 29 Aug.

annex_xlsx.note_why: The press release's own Excel annex in MoSPI's eSankhyiki catalogue, fetched automatically (cpi_annex.py). One table holds the base-2024 Combined index from Jan 2025, MoSPI's printed inflation from Jan 2026, and the provisional mark. Selected by its title, which states the base, never by annex number: 'Annex-IV' was a base-2012 state table until Dec 2025. Every listed release is saved (sha256 dedupes), so a missed month is recovered on the next run. Catalogue entries for Feb–Aug 2026 were all created 2026-10-01: whether the catalogue updates on release day is unmeasured until September's release (due ~13 Oct).

release_pdf.note_why: The monthly press release, read by hand with `fetch.py --cpi-pdf`. Kept as the fallback until the annex has been seen to land on release day; then retired with cpi_release.py. Releases Jan–Aug 2026 were saved from it.

dashboard_xlsx.note_why: The 'download data' workbook on MoSPI's CPI page, fetched automatically. It holds the base-2024 index back to Jan 2025, which gives CPI a year back so 1c can check MoSPI's printed inflation against the index. It lags the press release (on 2026-09-28 it still ended in July, dated 12 Aug), states no P/F flag and no base.

cpi.note_max_revision: A revision beyond 1% of the value fails. CPI revisions are ~0.01 index points (Jan 2026: 104.46 → 104.45); the workbook states no base, so a level jump between the two publications (a 2012-base series is ~200) must stop the run rather than warn.
cpi.note_why: The API holds only the 2012 base, ending Dec 2025 (base_year=2024 → 'No Data Found', re-probed 2026-09-28); it is never used. CPI is one dataset fed by two MoSPI publications (`sources`). Their releases merge in PUBLICATION order (`published`), not fetch order, because the workbook lags: fetched after the August release, it would otherwise overwrite July's final value with the provisional one. Lag: July 2026 was released 12 Aug.

note_currency_stage: The stage a dependent's gate runs first (core/gate.py, depends_on): the release calendar, so no credit pipeline computes 1f against MoSPI data that is overdue.
note_grace: Days past the declared lag before a missing period is overdue. MoSPI moves a release off a weekend (CPI for Aug 2026, nominally the 12th, came on the 15th), and releases land at 4 PM.
